limitations: Series of six dogs; only statements explicitly naming a dog, naming all dogs, or Table 1 rows are attributed to individuals. The analgesic sentence lists meloxicam, tramadol or buprenorphine for the dogs collectively; per-dog assignment is not stated, so each dog carries review-only possible items.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Discussion recurrence statements (two dogs with 2.2 and 2.4 cm exposure; recurrence with 2.5 cm and 3 cm protrusion) are not labelled by dog and their numbers do not match Table 1 protrusion lengths; not assigned to any dog.
Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.
Table 1 age column is not labelled as age at presentation, so age_other is used. Follow-up months in Table 1 are not linked to text time points such as re-examination 14 months after surgery.
The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.

The analgesic sentence lists meloxicam, tramadol or buprenorphine for the dogs collectively; per-dog assignment is not stated, so each dog carries review-only possible items.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Discussion recurrence statements (two dogs with 2.2 and 2.4 cm exposure; recurrence with 2.5 cm and 3 cm protrusion) are not labelled by dog and their numbers do not match Table 1 protrusion lengths; not assigned to any dog.
Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.
Table 1 age column is not labelled as age at presentation, so age_other is used. Follow-up months in Table 1 are not linked to text time points such as re-examination 14 months after surgery.
The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.
Figure pixels viewed at full resolution with zoomed panel crops in the separate visual submission; caption-layer figure entries stay not_inspected.

Parent review: the dog 5 recurrence statement in the Discussion is accepted as a literal dog-labelled fact (compatible with Table 1 and Results). Unlabelled Discussion sentences (two dogs with oedema attributed to lymphatic trauma; polyglactin 901 suture possibly contributing to recurrence, although the technique section names polypropylene) are not assigned to any dog.

claims.text: Dog 3, a castrated male Maltese aged 4.0 years and weighing 7.4 kg, had idiopathic paraphimosis with signs lasting 1 month. Examination upon presentation showed permanent penile protrusion, hyperaemia, and the penile protrusion measured 1.8 cm. The prepuce could easily be moved cranially to cover the protruded penis. The referring veterinarian had partially closed the preputial orifice with a purse-string suture for 6 days, resolving the paraphimosis, but it recurred 2 weeks after suture removal.

limitations: Series of six dogs; only statements explicitly naming a dog, naming all dogs, or Table 1 rows are attributed to individuals. Unlabelled narrative (complete blood counts and biochemistry within normal limits, radiograph and ultrasound workup, unlabelled surgical technique steps, meloxicam continued orally for 3 days, Elizabethan collar, pain scale, telephone follow-up) is not copied to every dog.
The analgesic sentence lists meloxicam, tramadol or buprenorphine for the dogs collectively; per-dog assignment is not stated, so each dog carries review-only possible items.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Discussion recurrence statements (two dogs with 2.2 and 2.4 cm exposure; recurrence with 2.5 cm and 3 cm protrusion) are not labelled by dog and their numbers do not match Table 1 protrusion lengths; not assigned to any dog.
Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.
Table 1 age column is not labelled as age at presentation, so age_other is used. Follow-up months in Table 1 are not linked to text time points such as re-examination 14 months after surgery.
The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.
Figure pixels viewed at full resolution with zoomed panel crops in the separate visual submission; caption-layer figure entries stay not_inspected.

Parent review: the dog 5 recurrence statement in the Discussion is accepted as a literal dog-labelled fact (compatible with Table 1 and Results). Unlabelled Discussion sentences (two dogs with oedema attributed to lymphatic trauma; polyglactin 901 suture possibly contributing to recurrence, although the technique section names polypropylene) are not assigned to any dog.

limitations: Series of six dogs; only statements explicitly naming a dog, naming all dogs, or Table 1 rows are attributed to individuals. Unlabelled narrative (complete blood counts and biochemistry within normal limits, radiograph and ultrasound workup, unlabelled surgical technique steps, meloxicam continued orally for 3 days, Elizabethan collar, pain scale, telephone follow-up) is not copied to every dog.
The analgesic sentence lists meloxicam, tramadol or buprenorphine for the dogs collectively; per-dog assignment is not stated, so each dog carries review-only possible items.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Discussion recurrence statements (two dogs with 2.2 and 2.4 cm exposure; recurrence with 2.5 cm and 3 cm protrusion) are not labelled by dog and their numbers do not match Table 1 protrusion lengths; not assigned to any dog.
Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.
Table 1 age column is not labelled as age at presentation, so age_other is used. Follow-up months in Table 1 are not linked to text time points such as re-examination 14 months after surgery.
The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.
Figure pixels viewed at full resolution with zoomed panel crops in the separate visual submission; caption-layer figure entries stay not_inspected.

Parent review: the dog 5 recurrence statement in the Discussion is accepted as a literal dog-labelled fact (compatible with Table 1 and Results). Unlabelled Discussion sentences (two dogs with oedema attributed to lymphatic trauma; polyglactin 901 suture possibly contributing to recurrence, although the technique section names polypropylene) are not assigned to any dog.

Parent review: the abstract statements "All dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery" and "All short-term complications resolved without treatment" are treated as imprecise cohort summaries (the Results counterpart is smooth recovery from anaesthesia), recorded as ambiguities rather than source-conflict pairs; dog-labelled Results and Table 1 complication facts stay included.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.

The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.

limitations: Series of six dogs; only statements explicitly naming a dog, naming all dogs, or Table 1 rows are attributed to individuals. Unlabelled narrative (complete blood counts and biochemistry within normal limits, radiograph and ultrasound workup, unlabelled surgical technique steps, meloxicam continued orally for 3 days, Elizabethan collar, pain scale, telephone follow-up) is not copied to every dog.
The analgesic sentence lists meloxicam, tramadol or buprenorphine for the dogs collectively; per-dog assignment is not stated, so each dog carries review-only possible items.

Abstract states four minor complications in three dogs while Table 1 lists six complication entries across dogs 1, 4 and 5; recorded as an arithmetic or categorisation mismatch, not a source conflict.

Abstract says all dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery and all short-term complications resolved without treatment, which sits uneasily with Results for dogs 1, 4 and 5; held as review-only items and ambiguities.
Outcome definitions (good if a minor complication was noted, excellent if free of clinical signs) do not obviously match the Table 1 grades for dogs 1 and 4; not reconciled.

Discussion recurrence statements (two dogs with 2.2 and 2.4 cm exposure; recurrence with 2.5 cm and 3 cm protrusion) are not labelled by dog and their numbers do not match Table 1 protrusion lengths; not assigned to any dog.
Median and range values in the Abstract and Results are cohort statistics and are not copied to individuals; Table 1 cells were used instead.
Table 1 age column is not labelled as age at presentation, so age_other is used. Follow-up months in Table 1 are not linked to text time points such as re-examination 14 months after surgery.
The orchidectomy of the left descended testicle sentence does not name a dog; it is held as a review-only item for dog 6 only.
Figure pixels viewed at full resolution with zoomed panel crops in the separate visual submission; caption-layer figure entries stay not_inspected.

Parent review: the dog 5 recurrence statement in the Discussion is accepted as a literal dog-labelled fact (compatible with Table 1 and Results). Unlabelled Discussion sentences (two dogs with oedema attributed to lymphatic trauma; polyglactin 901 suture possibly contributing to recurrence, although the technique section names polypropylene) are not assigned to any dog.

Parent review: the abstract statements "All dogs recovered uneventfully from surgery" and "All short-term complications resolved without treatment" are treated as imprecise cohort summaries (the Results counterpart is smooth recovery from anaesthesia), recorded as ambiguities rather than source-conflict pairs; dog-labelled Results and Table 1 complication facts stay included.
